CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Best practice when working on Athletics and Mosaic: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Athletics and Mosaic.
   B. Practise Athletics and Mosaic with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Athletics and Mosaic.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Athletics and Mosaic.

2. Best practice when working on Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games.
   C. Practise Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games.

3. Best practice when working on Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts : (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts .
   B. Damage equipment used for Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts .
   C. Disrupt classmates during Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts .
   D. Practise Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts  with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

4. Best practice when working on Components of Creative Arts and Sports: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Components of Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Components of Creative Arts and Sports.
   C. Damage equipment used for Components of Creative Arts and Sports.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Components of Creative Arts and Sports.

5. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.

6. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. Only the volume
   B. The ticket price
   C. Only the costume
   D. The speed of the music

7. Best practice when working on Melody: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Melody.
   B. Practise Melody with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Melody.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Melody.

8. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Red, blue, and yellow
   B. Black, white, and grey
   C. Green, orange, and purple
   D. Brown, pink, and gold

9. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Guarantee a trophy
   B. Remove the need for rules
   C. Replace drinking water
   D. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

10. Best practice when working on Careers in Creative Arts and Sports: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Careers in Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Careers in Creative Arts and Sports.
   C. Damage equipment used for Careers in Creative Arts and Sports.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Careers in Creative Arts and Sports.

11. Best practice when working on Swimming: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Swimming.
   B. Damage equipment used for Swimming.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Swimming.
   D. Practise Swimming with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. Best practice when working on Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal.
   B. Practise Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Rhythm and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Athletics and Mosaic and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Melody and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Rugby and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Practise Athletics and Mosaic with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

2. C — Practise Kenyan Indigenous Games Board games with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

3. D — Practise Swimming 10 2.12.2 Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts  with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

4. A — Practise Components of Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. A — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. D — The speed of the music

7. B — Practise Melody with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. A — Red, blue, and yellow

9. D — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

10. A — Practise Careers in Creative Arts and Sports with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

11. D — Practise Swimming with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. B — Practise Kenyan Indigenous Games 10 3.0 Appreciation in Creative Arts and Sports 3.1 Anal with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Melody; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Rugby; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
